title: Locally Nagata universal catenarity ascends along weakly etale maps
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:A\to B$ be weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the local ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is Nagata [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], and that $A$ is universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then $B$ is universally catenary and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ the local ring $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is Nagata. Here universally catenary means that every finite type algebra over the ring is catenary: between any fixed comparable primes the lengths of finite prime chains are bounded, and all saturated chains have the same length; a saturated chain admits no prime strictly between consecutive terms.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Mathematical Journal 60 (1976), 139–149, DOI 10.1017/S0027763000017190
source.place: Theorem 5.3(iii), printed pp. 146–147 (PDF pp. 8–9); proof on p. 147 through Proposition 5.4 and Lemma 5.5. Remark 5.2 for AF = weakly etale. Definitions: Stacks Tags 00NI (definition-catenary), 00NL (definition-universally-catenary), 032R (definition-nagata).

proof.text: For $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B$, put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Base change $A\to B$ to $A_{\mathfrak p}$ and then localize the target at the prime induced by $\mathfrak q$. The stability lemma and the weak etaleness of localization show that the resulting local map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ is weakly etale. Explicitly $(B\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p})_{\mathfrak q^{\prime}}\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$ by $b\otimes(a/s)\mapsto f(a)b/f(s)$; every denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ maps outside $\mathfrak q$. These localizations are Noetherian: every ideal is the extension of its contraction and fractions of finitely many generators of that contraction generate it.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Theorem 5.3(iii), first sentence of its proof; Stacks Tags 092H, 092J, 092N for the localized map.

proof.text: The hypothesis supplies that $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is Nagata. Apply Nagata ascent to the Noetherian weakly etale map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$ from step 1. Thus $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is Nagata for each $\mathfrak q$, proving the local Nagata assertion without assuming that $A$ itself is Nagata.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Theorem 5.3(iii), first sentence of its proof, and Remark 5.7(ii).

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and write $R=A[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, $S=B[X_1,\ldots,X_n]=R\otimes_A B$. Both are Noetherian by finite-type Noetherianity, and $R\to S$ is weakly etale by base change. Here the tensor identification sends $h(X)\otimes b$ to $f(h)(X)b$; its inverse sends $\sum b_\alpha X^\alpha$ to $\sum X^\alpha\otimes b_\alpha$, so both composites fix coefficients and variables. Every finite type $R$-algebra is finite type over $A$ (adjoin its generators together with the $X_i$), so $R$ is universally catenary. It is also locally Nagata: for a prime $\mathfrak r\subset R$ with contraction $\mathfrak a\subset A$, $R_{\mathfrak r}$ is a localization of $A_{\mathfrak a}[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$. Its coefficient ring is Nagata by hypothesis, the polynomial ring is Nagata by $n$ applications of polynomial Nagata permanence, and the localization is Nagata. The fraction identification sends $a/s$ to the same fraction and fixes each $X_i$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Proposition 5.4 and the polynomial reduction in the proof of Theorem 5.3(iii); Stacks Tags 00FN, 0334, 032U.

proof.text: For a weakly etale R-algebra S, fix two comparable primes with the same contraction p. Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.preimageOrderIsoFiber identifies them with comparable primes of p.Fiber S = kappa(p) tensor_R S. Base change preserves weak etaleness. Since a field is absolutely flat, Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' and Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.tfae in the proved source module WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.WeakDimension show that this fibre has Krull dimension at most zero. Every prime is maximal, so the two fibre primes coincide. The order isomorphism then identifies the original primes. Thus strict inclusions contract strictly. This avoids the separate weakly-etale-field theorem and any finiteness or algebraicity argument.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.3(iii), discreteness of fibres; Stacks Tag 092Q and the explicit algebraic-domain argument.

proof.text: Catenarity descends along any surjective ring map: inverse image is an order embedding of ideals, and every prime between two inverse images contains the kernel and hence is the inverse image of its image prime. Catenarity also passes to localizations: Mathlib IsLocalization.orderIsoOfPrime identifies prime ideals with the primes disjoint from the multiplicative set, and every prime between two such primes is disjoint because it is contained in the upper one. In each case contraction preserves strict prime chains, endpoints, lengths and saturation, giving both the chain-length bound and equality of saturated-chain lengths directly from IsCatenaryRing. For an essentially finite type R-algebra S, Mathlib Algebra.EssFiniteType.subalgebra and submonoid present it as a localization of a finite type R-subalgebra. If R is universally catenary that finite type subalgebra is catenary, hence so is S. Finite type algebras over an essentially finite type algebra are essentially finite type over R by composition; this proves universal catenarity for a Noetherian essentially finite type algebra. When the algebra and base have different universes, a polynomial presentation makes the algebra Small in the base universe; Shrink.algEquiv transports catenarity through the surjective equivalence. Thus the same-universe quantifier in IsUniversallyCatenary loses no cases.

source.place: Tags 00NJ (lemma-localization-catenary) and 00NI/00NL (definition-catenary/definition-universally-catenary); written out using the cited general prime correspondence and polynomial presentations.

proof.text: For consecutive primes P < Q of S let p and q be their contractions to R. Localize to Rprime = R_q and Sprime = S_Q using Localization.localRingHom. Composition with localization preserves weak etaleness, and a compatible tensor equivalence over a localization of the base proves weak etaleness over Rprime, in mixed universes as well. Let a = p Rprime, c = P Sprime and b = a Sprime. The localization ideal order embedding proves that a and c are prime, their contractions are p and P, and c contracts to a; therefore b is contained in c. Set C = Rprime/a, D = Sprime/b. C is a Noetherian local domain and D a Noetherian local ring, with nontriviality following from b being contained in the prime c. The tensor-quotient equivalence Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor makes C to D a base change of Rprime to Sprime, hence weakly etale. It is local since both the localized map and the quotient maps reflect units. Essential finite type permanence from step 5 makes C universally catenary. The Nagata hypothesis at q directly gives that C is Japanese; isN1_of_isN2 therefore supplies the finite normalization of C needed by the local component dimension theorem.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.3(iii), applying Lemma 5.5 to consecutive contracted primes; Stacks Tags 00CT, 032T.

proof.text: Let J be the image of c in D. Quotient ideal correspondence makes J prime and its contraction to C zero. If a prime K were strictly below J, step 4 applied to C to D would give a prime strictly below zero in C. Hence J is minimal. The localization prime correspondence transfers the original adjacency of P < Q to the absence of a prime strictly between c and the maximal ideal of Sprime. In Sprime/c, every nonzero prime therefore contracts to the maximal ideal and is maximal, giving Ring.KrullDimLE 1. Apply lem-exc-weakly-etale-local-component-dimension to C to D and J: dim(D/J) = dim C. DoubleQuot.quotQuotEquivQuotOfLE identifies D/J with Sprime/c, so dim C is at most one. An intermediate prime between p and q would localize to a prime strictly between a and the maximal ideal of Rprime; its image in C would be a nonzero nonmaximal prime, contradicting Ring.KrullDimLE 1. Thus contractions of adjacent primes are adjacent. The proof needs only a dimension upper bound, not a separate proof that the dimension is exactly one.

source.place: Lemma 5.5 and its application in the proof of Theorem 5.3(iii), printed p. 147; Stacks Tag 00E3 for localization prime correspondence.

proof.text: For each interval of prime ideals of S, compose a finite prime chain with contraction. Step 4 preserves strictness and length, and steps 6 and 7 preserve saturation. Applying the chain bound and saturated-chain equality for the contracted endpoints in R gives both clauses of IsCatenaryRing S directly. No choice of maximal refinements is needed. Empty spectra and chains of length zero are covered by the same quantified argument.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), online copy
source.place: Conclusion of the saturated-chain argument in the proof of Theorem 5.3(iii).

proof.text: Every finite type $B$-algebra is a quotient of some $B[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$, which is catenary by steps 3–8. Such a quotient is catenary: primes of $S/J$ correspond by inverse image to primes of $S$ containing $J$; every prime between two such primes also contains $J$, so the corresponding intervals and their saturated chains agree exactly. The same chain bounds and lengths apply. Thus all finite type $B$-algebras are catenary, which is universal catenarity of $B$. Together with step 2 this proves both assertions.
